title: TrailGenic Metabolic Flexibility Adaptation Dataset
description: Shell dataset module for TrailGenic physiology adaptation science modeling the development of metabolic flexibility through endurance training and fasted exercise exposure.

records.mechanism: Substrate switching capacity progressively deepens under sustained fasted altitude protocol exposure

stimulus.measurement_model: multi-point breath ketone capture across wake, end-effort, and recovery windows

physiological_response: Wake ketones trended from 1.1 ppm baseline (November 2025) to 3.9 ppm peak (April 2026)
End-effort ketones reached 22 ppm post-summit record (San Jacinto, April 11, 2026)
Multi-day retention sustained to 4.7 ppm Day-1 after apex effort
adaptation_outcomes: Substrate switching depth at autophagy-relevant range
Multi-day signaling persists into recovery window

supporting_science.finding: Fasted endurance training can increase reliance on fat oxidation and alter substrate availability during exercise.
Metabolic flexibility reflects the capacity to switch between lipid and carbohydrate oxidation in response to demand.

records.mechanism: Improved substrate switching between carbohydrate and fat metabolism

supporting_science.finding: Metabolic flexibility is strongly linked to cardiometabolic health and is improved through exercise training.

physiological_response: enhanced fatty acid transport into mitochondria
adaptation_outcomes: reduced metabolic stress during prolonged exercise

supporting_science.finding: Endurance training increases mitochondrial enzyme activity and oxidative capacity in skeletal muscle.
